output.myth: Mesket kept the watch on the north cliff, where the wind comes first. She did not look at the sea. She looked at the gulls. When they turned over the bay all at once, like a sheet shaken out, she called the boats in. Her eyes had gone grey from the salt, and she said that was why she could see it. The Gulls told her things, she said, and she did not argue with them. One autumn they turned and turned and would not settle, so she called the boats, and the boats came in. Tavo came down the bay that night laughing. He tore three nets off the poles and took nothing that could be bargained back. Mesket was not thanked, and she was not blamed. When she died they flew her up as a kite with a grey cloth tail. She still hangs over the Reach, facing the cold, turning when the gulls turn. Mend your net. Watch the bay.
output.verse:
Gulls turn on the bay
Mesket reads the cold north wind
Mend the net; keep watch
